notes: Two of the turn's stance tags, `threshold` (PRESSURED) and `counterforce` (DS-ECO-6), are not defined anywhere in the brief, which names only three stances: ledger, street, visitor. I had to guess what they colour.

The brief contradicts itself on whether a spine may be attributed. The STANCE section says `spine` is ALWAYS the bare fact on the document's own authority; the VOICE section says a spine may be carried by the public or a source and that a pool's three spines take three different shapes. I wrote bare spines except one carried by the public, which may breach whichever rule is authoritative.

Every pool says `faces to write: 0` and `notebook: none`, so the whole page is seven spines with no faces. Most of the brief (seating, pairs, compromised roles, the weighing, the face count per seated source, the sibling-distinctness rules) then has nothing to act on, and it is unclear whether the page-level quotas that are written per page rather than per unit still bind, in particular the one-physical-particular rule and the at-most-two-weighings rule.

The rule that a second sentence must rest on a listed field and name it in its own word is hard to satisfy where the listed fields are null or are bare identifiers. DS-ECO-1 lists only `prosperityRank = null`, yet the corpus claim I must keep names a working road and a working market, neither of which is a listed field; DS-GEN-18 lists five fields that are all null. I kept the corpus claim and accepted the risk.

Several corpus lines breach the stated bars, which the brief anticipates but which leaves the claim ambiguous: DS-ECO-12's income-mix spine uses `you will be given` (future indicative plus address to the reader) and DS-GEN-18's uses a semicolon and the phrase `the books`, which the brief separately bars as naming nothing on the roster. Also, that pool's title says two or three income sources while its field says ten rows.

The 'second sentence must rest on one of the FIELDS and name it in its own word' instruction is ambiguous about whether the field's word must appear literally in the second sentence itself or just ground the unit topically; I read it as the latter where a literal restatement would have produced a summarising-close (a taste fault under ruling 34).

Pool key 'INCOME MIX: two or three sources between them' (DS-ECO-12 vid 2) names 'two or three' but the only FIELDS value given is incomeSources.length = 10 (FROZEN) - the two numbers don't reconcile, and since floor 2 bars invented counts I stated neither number, matching the corpus line's own vague 'short list' framing instead.

For 'TIER: minor shadow activity (≥3)' (DS-ECO-6) the only live field is blackMarketCapture = 8, but no typed slot is declared to print it, so under the floor-2 rule (a number is lawful only where a typed slot prints it from a named field) I omitted the value entirely; the resulting note carries no quantitative grounding beyond the corpus line's own qualitative claim.

'PRESSURED' (DS-ECO-9) explicitly instructs 'write ONE sentence and no second' because no fields are recorded, which conflicts with the corpus fallback line's own two-sentence shape; I followed the explicit one-sentence instruction rather than the corpus line's structure.

Whether 'the books wait' (STALLED, DS-GEN-18) counts as an unlicensed generic-record citation ('never the books as a generic') was unclear, since it describes physical ledgers sitting idle rather than citing them as an attributed authority ('the books have it that...'); I treated it as descriptive furniture already licensed by the corpus line's own claim, not a new citation.

Every pool's listed FIELDS value was null (LIVE or FROZEN alike), so there was never a legitimate value to hang a second sentence on; I resolved this by writing one (possibly compound) sentence per unit throughout rather than guessing a field value, which also sidesteps the 'second sentence must rest on a field' requirement entirely.

The mechanical-bars list (brief.md lines 6-12) never names the colon as barred, but PART V (notebook) lists the colon as a device the fair copy specifically lacks; several corpus fallback lines (ADMINISTERED, scores.monster) use a colon on the player page, which reads as a contradiction between the exemplar pack's own fallback text and the notebook-exclusivity rule inferred from PART V.

Multiple corpus fallback lines break bars the brief itself states elsewhere: semicolons (MARKET-OPEN, scores.magical, the 'ordinary' pool), a which-clause close (economicViability, foodSecurity), 'will'/'will not' (prominentRelationship), and a four-item list past the stated three-item ceiling (flagDriven) - all had to be silently rewritten under 'do not imitate the breach,' which is workable but means the fallback text supplied in-turn is frequently non-compliant with its own governing document.

This turn's audience is 'dm' and the brief describes a DM-only notebook register in detail, but every pool here declares zero dm-only rows, so the notebook machinery (shades, feelings, the six-bar register) is entirely unexercised by this card - nothing in the turn distinguishes a dm render from a player render.

The turn's 'stance' tags include elder, counterforce, and unfolding, but brief.md's own inventory of stance/spine-line tags names only three (ledger, street, visitor - 'THE THREE OLD STANCES ... SURVIVE AS THE SPINE LINE'S TAG'); the other three tags appear with no definition anywhere in the system prompt, so their intended effect on a bare spine's phrasing had to be inferred rather than looked up.

Two pools on one page carry opposite claims: DS-GEN-5 'ordinary' says the road's traffic passes and the town takes very little from it, while DS-GEN-6 'road' says everything the town cannot grow comes in on the road and the road is a condition of the town. Both were kept as given, so the page contradicts itself.

The page is audience dm, but every pool declares 'notebook: none', so the whole dm register the brief builds (PART V, the shades and feelings) has nowhere to appear. Unclear whether an empty notebook on a dm page is intended or a card defect.

The rule 'the second sentence must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word' is unusable on most pools here: every field value is null, and on three pools the only field is name = "Spitzplatz". Every unit was therefore written as a single sentence, which flattens the page's rhythm.

The pool key 'defenseProfile.readiness.label: Well-Defended' is itself the posture badge word the brief forbids naming, and the brief also says to write to the pool key's band. Resolved by writing the sense and never the word, but the two instructions conflict on their face.

Three stance tags used here (elder, unfolding, counterforce) are not among the three stances the brief defines (ledger, street, visitor), and the town seats no elders source at all, so 'elder' has no role to speak through. Several corpus lines also breach the brief's own bars (semicolons, a colon, a which-clause close, and 'will and will not do' against ruling 33), so the claim was kept and the wording refused.

Three pools were omitted as unwritable, not skipped: DS-DEF-2 'Invasion & War: walls with NO force' seats face 0 through `elders`, and DS-DEF-2 'Internal Security' (face 5) and DS-DEF-2 'Economic Survival: STRONG' (face 1) seat a face through `garrison`. The town block lists no roster for either source (sources = court, gate, guild, hall, market, public, register, stranger, tavern, watch; forceBuckets.garrison = false), and the turn forbids any other role at that position while the brief forbids trimming or reordering faces. The card and the seating disagree with each other.

The brief's STANCE section says the spine is always the bare fact in the archiver's own hand, but the VOICE section says a spine may be carried by the public or a source, and several supplied corpus spines are attributed ('A drover says...', 'The hall holds that...'). I wrote every spine bare, on ruling 40, but the two instructions read as contradictory.

The rule that a unit's second sentence 'must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word' is stricter than the pool key itself: for 'readiness ADEQUATE' the only field is a score I am forbidden to number, and for 'structure organized' no fields are recorded at all. I wrote single-sentence spines throughout rather than guess which word counts as naming a score.

The DM-audience instruction and the per-pool instruction conflict in form: the page is audience `dm`, which the brief says carries the archiver's notebook, but every pool says 'notebook: none. Return an empty list.' I followed the per-pool line and returned empty notebooks everywhere, so nothing on this page uses the notebook register the brief spends PART V defining.

Two smaller gaps. 'stance' (threshold, street, visitor, counterforce, ledger, unfolding) is given per pool but the brief only describes ledger/street/visitor, leaving threshold, counterforce and unfolding undefined. And the 'WRITE THE FILL, NOT THE TOKEN' block for 'Invasion & War' declares a {court} fill while the slot line above it says 'slots you may use: (none)'.

Pool 'riskLabel: Holding' declares {seat} and {faction} with the SAME fill ('Guild Council'), so its own corpus line renders as the Council holding because the Council is the heavier of the two. I used the seat alone and dropped the faction slot.

Two pools give a recorded field as a raw code expression (`readings.politics ?? null.blocs = null`; a ternary ending `.govMultiplier = null`). Both are null and both are raw identifiers the mechanical bars forbid on the page, so the rule 'a second sentence must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word' could not be met; I wrote one sentence for each.

Audience is dm, yet every pool says 'notebook: none. Return an empty list.' The dm page therefore comes out identical to the player page, and PART V of the brief has nothing to act on. Unclear whether that is intended for this tab.

Every pool says 'faces to write: 0', so nearly all of the brief and the whole exemplar pack (source roles, pairs, weighings, compromised roles, the public) has no surface to apply to. It was unclear whether a spine-only page is still expected to carry any of the attribution apparatus, or is strictly the bare fact.

Several corpus lines are simultaneously 'the claim you must keep' and breaches of the stated bars (two carry a semicolon, one a which-clause, one a summarising close). I kept the claims and did not imitate the breaches, per the brief, but the conflict is worth naming.

Omitted 3 of 15 pools (DS-DEF-2: 'Invasion & War: walls with NO force' vid 3, 'Internal Security: full legal chain (court AND prison)' vid 3, 'Economic Survival: STRONG' vid 3): each mandates a face spoken through 'elders' or 'garrison', but town.md's roles/sources arrays seat neither (forceBuckets.garrison is false and armedForces has no garrison key at all; 'elders' has a holder entry but no roster under roles). Brief.md's own bar ('every role phrase you use must be one this town seats') and omission rule make these unwritable as specified, so they fall to the hand corpus.

The turn's per-pool 'stance' values include threshold, counterforce and unfolding; brief.md only defines three stances (ledger/street/visitor). I inferred a fitting register for the undefined ones from pool context rather than from any stated rule.

Two corpus fallback lines given as 'the claim to keep' themselves breach bars the brief says not to imitate: WALLED-STRAINED's corpus spine ends on a which-clause closer, and 'walls PRESENT'/'arcane defense PRESENT' use a colon (a device the brief licenses only in the DM notebook, never on the fair copy). I kept the claims but rewrote around the breaches.

Brief.md's STANCE section states the spine is 'always... bare, on the document's own authority,' but several corpus spines for this very turn (Disasters & Famine; charter hall PRESENT) are themselves attributed accounts ('A drover says...', 'A stranger... finds...'). I followed each pool's own corpus shape over the blanket 'always bare' statement.

'structure organized' (DS-DEF-4) declares no fields recorded and instructs exactly ONE sentence, while its corpus fallback line is two sentences carrying more claim detail; I condensed to one lawful sentence per the turn's explicit instruction rather than the corpus's shape.

The {institution} fill is "Cartographer's guild", but the town block's institution roster lists "Cartographer's workshop" and its sources list seats no guild at all. I wrote the fill as the turn instructed, but the fill and the card contradict each other.

Every pool says "faces to write: 0" and "notebook: none", so the page is spines only. Most of the brief (one face per seated source, the pairs, the weighing, the compromised role, the public, the notebook's whole PART V) had nothing to apply to, and the audience being dm with zero notebook rows looks like a contradiction between the turn and the brief's DM register section.

The rule that a second sentence "must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word" is hard to satisfy where every listed value is null or an opaque row count (prosperityRank = null, readings = null, incomeSources = "[4 rows]"). Naming such a field in its own word risks asserting a value the card does not carry, which the same brief refuses.

The corpus fallback lines breach bars the brief enforces: a colon in DS-ECO-1 and a semicolon in DS-GEN-18. I kept the claims without imitating the breaches, but it leaves the fallback that ships on refusal unlawful by the brief's own mechanical list.

The DS-ECO-12 income claim cites "the accounts", which is the record-citation shape the brief warns raises a shrink-only ceiling, and the town's treasury holder is SOURCE-UNRESOLVED. I kept the claim without the citation. Separately, "well past half" is a magnitude the claim requires while floor 2 bars invented numbers; I carried it in words because the corpus line already does.

Several pools say fields are unrecorded so the spine must be ONE sentence, but the corpus-line fallback for those same pools (DS-POW-2 recentConflict, DS-POW-7 layer DORMANT) uses a semicolon, and DS-POW-1's prosperity line uses a which-clause closer; the brief says not to imitate a corpus breach but never reconciles that with matching the corpus line's own two-clause shape, so the rewrite required a judgment call not specified in the rules.

DS-POW-4 'legitimacyHold: public backing hardens the hold' prints its field as what reads like literal source code (a ternary/optional-chaining expression ending '...govMultiplier = null') rather than a resolved field name and value, so it is unclear which name a second sentence should cite, and the resolved value (null) carries no narrative content to build one from; I wrote one sentence and skipped the optional second rather than guess.

The turn's stance labels for this tab (unfolding, visitor, street, counterforce) don't match the brief's own named stance family ([ledger]/[street]/[visitor]); 'unfolding' and 'counterforce' are undefined in the brief, so their intended effect on wording beyond thematic hinting is not documented.

DS-POW-2 'recentConflict present' gives a live field whose text embeds a duration ('for three months'); the brief licenses a number only where 'a typed slot prints it in words from that field,' but doesn't say whether a duration embedded in free-text field content counts as such a slot, so I omitted the count as the safer reading rather than being told to.

Two pools (DS-POW-1 'Approved' and DS-POW-4 'riskLabel: Holding') give {seat} and {faction} the identical value 'Guild Council,' which the corpus line's own wording uses twice in one sentence, reading as a tautology if both fills are inserted literally; the brief doesn't say whether a pronoun may stand in for a repeated slot value, so I used one for readability.

Pool SECURE (DS-ECO-9) instructs "write ONE sentence and no second" but its own corpus-line fallback is two sentences - a direct contradiction; I resolved it as one compound sentence with "and" to keep the claim while honoring the one-sentence instruction.

Pool STALLED (DS-GEN-18) fills {institution} as "Cartographer's guild", but town.md's institution roster only lists "Cartographer's workshop" (category: crafts) - no guild by that name is a row this town's card carries, so the given slot fill does not match the town data it is supposed to be drawn from.

STALLED's corpus-line fallback cites "the books" as a generic record, which the brief explicitly forbids ("never 'the books' as a generic"); I substituted "the accounts" since this town's holders list does carry a treasury, which the brief licenses by name.

COMBINATION C3's corpus-line fallback uses a colon, but the brief reserves colon punctuation for the DM notebook register only ("licensed on dm-only faces only") and elsewhere warns not to imitate a colon breach in the corpus line - I rewrote it comma-joined to stay lawful on the player page.

The boilerplate rule "the second sentence of a unit, if there is one, must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word" appears on every pool verbatim, including ones where every listed field is null/FROZEN (C3, STALLED); it is unclear whether that means no second sentence is licensed at all in those cases, since the given corpus-line fallbacks themselves add descriptive content that doesn't literally name any field.
